confirmed_criteria.name: Completeness vs RFP Requirements
confirmed_criteria.description: Every explicit RFP requirement is addressed.
confirmed_criteria.why: The RFP lists seven numbered requirements and puts each one in bold. A buyer who writes a checklist reads the answer as a checklist.

evaluation.summary: The functional scope matches the RFP well, but pricing and dates aren’t committed, and support terms and risks are missing.

rationales.completeness_vs_rfp: Requirements 1–4 are covered, 5 only partly, 6 and 7 not at all.
rationales.risk_assumptions_transparency: No risks or assumptions, although both price and schedule depend on “discovery” and “integration complexity”.
rationales.pricing_clarity: A €70,000–€110,000 range instead of a price. The low end is below the client’s range, and it’s unclear whether Year 1 support is included.
rationales.timeline_clarity: Phases are named but have no dates. “Within the timeframe you’ve outlined” repeats the ask instead of committing to it.
rationales.data_accuracy_validation: Phased onboarding is meant to reduce disruption, but nothing says how the dashboard figures are checked against the current stock records before a site goes live.
rationales.problem_understanding: Names the 6 warehouses and the spreadsheet plus legacy setup. Doesn’t pick up the “minimal disruption” goal.
rationales.scope_deliverables_clarity: All four functional requirements are described specifically, including site-level roles and the no-migration constraint. Support and exclusions aren’t defined.
rationales.tone_persuasiveness: Clear and client-specific in the solution; the closing claim has no names, numbers or outcomes.
rationales.legacy_system_spreadsheets: The spreadsheets and the legacy system are named in the understanding, but the proposal never says what happens to them after go-live.

findings.rationale: Warehouses will be onboarded “in phases”, but not in what order, when, or how disruption is avoided.
findings.suggested_fix: Turn the rollout bullet into a short plan: the pilot site and why, the order of the other 5 sites, and a parallel run with the existing spreadsheets before each cutover.

findings.rationale: Support after go-live isn’t mentioned, nor whether the price covers the first year of support the budget includes.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a “Support & maintenance” section: response times by severity, support hours, and confirmation that Year 1 support is included in the price.

findings.rationale: No risks or assumptions are documented.
findings.suggested_fix: Add “Risks & assumptions”. The price depends on “integration complexity”, so name what drives it (schema quality, access rights) and what happens to cost and dates if discovery finds problems.

findings.rfp_quote: €80,000–€120,000 total, including first year of support
findings.rationale: A €70,000–€110,000 range with a firm quote after discovery. The low end is below the client’s range and Year 1 support isn’t stated as included.
findings.suggested_fix: Give one estimated total inside €80,000–€120,000 with a line-item breakdown including Year 1 support, and state the maximum change after discovery (for example ±10%).

findings.rfp_quote: Working pilot at one warehouse within 3 months
findings.rationale: Discovery, pilot and rollout are named with no dates attached.
findings.suggested_fix: Date each phase, for example: discovery Weeks 1–3, pilot live at one site by Week 12, all 6 sites by Week 24.

findings.rationale: Credentials without evidence. “Several mid-size distribution companies” gives the client nothing to verify.
findings.suggested_fix: Name one comparable project, anonymised if needed: number of sites, database, time to go-live.
